solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Despicable person holds Penny enthralled

indicators.note: a person who holds something keeps it inside, so the rascal's letters enclose the coin

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A villain keeps a woman called Penny spellbound in his grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is just the coin's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone utterly absorbed or spellbound is enthralled.

clue.text: Withdrawn, it's returned in new packaging

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it
packaging wraps round contents, so the fresh word encloses the short one

parts.note: something recent is new

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the two letters of it are read in reverse

parts.note: it's is read as it is, so the pronoun's two letters are taken as written

explanation.surface: A shy person's item is sent back in fresh wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone reserved and quiet, not revealing their thoughts, is withdrawn.

clue.text: Spectrum initially discovered in proper optical glass

indicators.note: one letter set in another word goes inside it

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper and correct

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the word Spectrum

explanation.surface: A rainbow was first found in a correct piece of lens glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is a link: the letter is found within the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a triangular block of glass that splits light into colours is an optical device.

clue.text: Required fellow to go out with daughter

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to go out with someone romantically is to date them

explanation.surface: A father insists a young man must take his daughter out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something mandated is officially ordered, so obligatory.

clue.text: Scrape away a beard, roughly

indicators.note: roughly suggests an untidy rearrangement, so the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Shaving off facial hair in a rough and ready way.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to wear a surface down by friction is to scrape it away.

clue.text: Decline to discourage what speaker does when one's interrupted

indicators.note: one letter interrupts the pair of words, so it is inserted between them

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
a public speaker orates, delivering a speech
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Refusing to put off a speaker who is cut short mid-speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse, but it is the verb meaning to worsen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to decline in quality or condition is to get worse over time.

clue.text: Severe suffering of soldiers in damaging action

indicators.note: the troops are set in the legal wrong, so its letters go inside

parts.note: a tort is a wrongful act causing harm, in law
men is a common term for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops caught up in destructive fighting endure great hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: great mental or physical anguish is torment.

clue.text: In need of cleaning but son's avoided responsibility

indicators.note: the son is avoided, kept out, so his letter leaves the dirty word

parts.note: something dusty needs cleaning
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: The room is filthy, but the son has shirked his chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an obligation one is bound to carry out is a responsibility.

clue.text: One off travelling — he's deserted Jack, perhaps

indicators.note: deserted means left, so the pronoun's letters go missing from the killer's name

parts.note: Jack the Ripper is the Victorian murderer, here given by his epithet
he's is read as he has, so the pronoun is what leaves

explanation.surface: A traveller has abandoned his companion Jack on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack, perhaps' points to Jack the Ripper; the epithet loses HE. A tripper is British for someone on a day trip or excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a holidaymaker on a short outing, someone who is off on their travels.

clue.text: Peter Parrot murdered? This one did the deed

indicators.note: murdered words are mangled, so these two names are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whodunit: Peter Parrot has been killed and someone here did it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits a crime or deed is the one responsible for carrying it out.

clue.text: Card sent back to desert

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert them

explanation.surface: A card is returned with orders to abandon the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun of sand but is the verb, giving RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of the picture cards in a fortune-telling pack.

clue.text: Dare America to go all out for brotherhood

indicators.note: letters that go all out are wildly thrown about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A challenge to the United States to make a supreme effort for fraternal unity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: comradeship and friendly fellowship within a group is brotherhood.

clue.text: Bank gift of money without fail

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the money word goes round the other

parts.note: a grant is a sum of money given
to die is to fail, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: A bank gives a cash present that is guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial but means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bank is a slope of ground, and a slope's steepness is its incline.

clue.text: Sleep with chap in Italian resort

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
Les is a man's name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: A holiday dozing beside some fellow in a sunny Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the southern Italian port city on its bay is a well-known resort.

clue.text: Something desirable on mature bird's feathers

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: a plum job or role is something very desirable
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A prized thing sits on the feathers of an older bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's coat of feathers taken together is called its plumage.

clue.text: Bill has problem keeping time

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so the puzzle's letters surround the abbreviation

parts.note: a poser is a difficult problem

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill struggles with a problem of punctuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but means a printed notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bill posted on a wall is a printed advertisement or placard.

clue.text: We backed out of the wrong gathering

indicators.note: the reversed pair is taken out of the phrase, leaving the rest
backed means turned back, so the two letters of We are read in reverse

explanation.surface: We retreated from the wrong crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large crowd of people gathered together is a throng.

clue.text: Spontaneously broken asunder here

definitions.note: adverb in the clue, read as 'done spontaneously' for the adjective

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these two words are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Something has suddenly been split apart at this very spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrehearsed is done off the cuff, without preparation, which is acting spontaneously.

clue.text: Electrical discharge beam kills primarily

parts.note: a spar is a pole or beam, as on a ship

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of kills

explanation.surface: A deadly electrical surge strikes mainly through a ray of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief flash of current jumping across a gap is a familiar kind of discharge.

clue.text: Bird nesting in hibiscus

indicators.note: the bird sits nesting in the plant's name, its letters tucked inside

explanation.surface: A bird making its nest in a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-legged wading bird with a down-curved bill.

clue.text: British endure forceful attack

parts.note: to last is to endure or continue

explanation.surface: The British hold out under a fierce assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a blast can be a violent burst or onslaught, as of wind or criticism.

clue.text: Perform in theatre with heartless take on Tosca say

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: Puccini's Tosca is an example of an opera

indicators.note: a heartless word has its middle removed, leaving just the outside letters of the word take

explanation.surface: A director plans a cold, unfeeling new production of Puccini's Tosca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests the stage, but here it is the operating theatre of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon working in an operating theatre carries out surgery, which is to operate.

clue.text: Cheapest accommodation always included in part of development

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting within it, so the poetic word goes inside

parts.note: a stage is one phase in a process of development
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Budget lodging is a permanent feature in some housing scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: On a passenger ship the lowest-priced berths, below decks, were known as the steerage.

clue.text: Be waiting around Gatwick finally for take-off

indicators.note: the waiting word goes around, so its letters enclose the single letter

parts.note: to sit around is to wait

indicators.note: finally picks out the very last letter of the airport's name

explanation.surface: Passengers hang about at Gatwick airport until their flight finally leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take-off' suggests a plane departing but means a parody. Gatwick is a London airport.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a comic imitation, a short sketch parodying someone or something.
